result.title: Knowledge transfer between simple discrete worlds
result.summary: Adapting to a new world and reasoning correctly about which outcomes are possible under rules one has not met before is a basic capacity underlying general intelligence. We study it in small discrete worlds: sets of grid configurations consistent with a shared set of rules, concretely Sudoku-like puzzles built from a common base and a handful of extra rules. We train a single depth-recurrent model on many combinations of rules and test it at four levels of novelty: a new puzzle, a new combination of known rules, a pairing of rules never seen together, and a rule instance not seen at all during training. The model receives the active rules either as a symbolic description or as two solved examples, and a model that gets no rule information is used as a baseline. At recombining rules it was trained on, the description matches or exceeds examples ($99\%$ against $95\%$ on new combinations). On rule instances whose components never co-occurred in training, the description falls below the no-information baseline while examples stay above it. The framework allows us to test many such generalization regimes in more systematic way than benchmarks such as ARC-AGI and provides new ground for evaluating depth-recurrent reasoning models, which are typically tested on saturated Sudoku benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在小规模离散网格世界（由共同基座加若干额外规则构成的类数独谜题）上训练单一深度循环模型，按四级新颖度测试规则迁移，并比较符号规则描述、两个已解样例与无规则信息基线三种输入条件。
AI.relevance_reason: 其深度循环推理模型、以及用「描述／样例／无信息基线」对比来检验规则信息是否真被使用、跨规则组合泛化的评测框架，可能为 LVR 的循环状态更新、视觉或规则旁路与贡献分配、长度泛化提供可核查线索。
